why: a static product fact. The simplest shape there is, and the one 51 of 60 settled gold goals have.
does the seller sell such a thing at all. INFORMATION with a referent that is NOT this listing — the scope is the goal's, and no component decides a search scope ahead of the resolver.
where is my order. STATE_READ, and the entity resolver names its own fields — the goal names none.
cancel it. The customer asked for external state to change, so this is the one shape that may reach a procedure.
MANDATORY. Asks only whether cancelling is possible. A DECISION, and no ACTION may be invented behind it — the procedure registry must not be consulted at all.

MANDATORY — this is C6. An out-of-window exchange approval is asked for; the exchange itself is not. One goal, DECISION, and the procedure registry is unreachable by construction rather than by instruction.

goals.explicit_request: 기한이 지났는데 교환 승인해주실 수 있나요?

customer_message_why: customer_message is WRITTEN, not assembled from the goals below. A join of two explicit_requests is a sentence nobody sent, and a smoke input has to be a thing a customer could have typed. Two requests joined by 그리고 — a plain conjunction, deliberately not a conditional, because a conditional here would tempt a FALLBACK relation that this row's gold does not carry.

why: variant compatibility. The goal says nothing about options; the KNOWLEDGE resolver decides that the answer depends on one and asks for it. Customer-input ownership, demonstrated rather than asserted.

MANDATORY. The connector cannot read this order. The GOAL IS UNCHANGED — still a STATE_READ of the order — and the runtime reports the registry's gap. No authority is substituted, and in particular the seller is not.

MANDATORY. No written policy decides this exception, so a new seller judgment is genuinely required. The interpreter did not put SELLER in the goal — the loop reached it from an OBSERVED absence, which is the difference between a required judgment and a fallback router.

goals.explicit_request: 이번 건만 예외로 반품 받아주실 수 있나요?

why: a referent this deployment cannot identify. The customer asks about an item they bought somewhere else: it is not this listing, not in the seller's catalogue and not an order, so there is nothing for any resolver to be about. The goal is real and the subject is not bound, so the loop settles at a gap instead of answering about the nearest thing it has. NOTE (v3.5 §D/E): this row previously read '러브 10P는 유리인가요?'. That sentence belongs to R:f403e606, which the same package adjudicated as INFORMATION about SELLER_CATALOGUE — a product the customer names is something the catalogue resolver can go and look for, and finding nothing is an outcome of looking rather than a subject nobody could identify. Leaving it here would have taught the smoke corpus the opposite of the gold.

goals.explicit_request: 다른 데서 산 어댑터가 있는데 이거랑 같이 쓸 수 있나요?
goals.subject: UNRESOLVED
goals.evidence: 다른 데서 산 어댑터가 있는데 이거랑 같이 쓸 수 있나요?

why: a procedure that cannot start until the order has been read. The ONLY legal chaining in this architecture, and it runs backwards from a plan: the prerequisite is named by the resolver that just ran, after running.

S:T12a. A DECISION whose policy cannot be applied until the order's fulfilment state is observed, and the observation SUCCEEDS. Before the resume rule this settled RESOLVED on the order read and the decision was never evaluated — the loop answered a question nobody asked and called it resolved.

why: the same shape with no registered policy: the decision rule needs the state, the state is observed, the rule is still absent, and only THEN is a new seller judgment genuinely required. The seller is reached from an observed absence that could not even be established until the state was read.

goals.explicit_request: 기한이 지났는데 교환 승인해주실 수 있나요?
goals.subject: CURRENT_ORDER
goals.evidence: 기한이 지났는데 교환 승인해주실 수 있나요?

why: S:T10b. 'I bought it thinking it was a bundle and only one arrived.' The interpreter's ONLY output is one INFORMATION goal about the listing: whether the delivered quantity matches what the listing offers. It does not invent a resend, a refund, a compensation or an order action — the customer asked none of them. If the evidence later shows a real fulfilment defect, that is a new Case raised from observed operational state, not a future action this interpreter manufactured from a complaint.

goals.explicit_request: 묶음 상품인 줄 알고 샀는데 한 개만 왔어요
goals.subject: CURRENT_LISTING

why: S:N2. 'Please issue a tax invoice.' An ACTION, and this registry has no procedure that is about an organization at all — PROCEDURE.ORDER_ACTION is order-scoped. The loop reports the registry's limit and asks NOBODY: in particular it does not quietly become an INFORMATION goal answered from KNOWLEDGE.ORG, which would answer a question the customer did not ask. Capability availability does not change what was requested.

B, D, H. A procedure that cannot start until the order has been read, and the read SUCCEEDS. The procedure is heard from again — the order read is not the answer to 'change my address' — and the goal ends where an action goal must end in a registry with no executor.

C, and the stale case specifically. The decision rule needs the order state; what came back was observed but not provably current. A stale row may be cited with its date and may never be stated as now, so the read did not close and the rule cannot be applied to it. The waiter is not resumed and the goal carries the registry's own reason.

goals.explicit_request: 주문했는데 받는 곳 주소를 바꿀 수 있나요?
goals.subject: CURRENT_ORDER
goals.evidence: 주문했는데 받는 곳 주소를 바꿀 수 있나요?

why: C, in the shape that was still live at 09f34a28. The prerequisite RAN and found nothing written down — NEEDS_SELLER, not a gap — and the earlier fix only stopped the resume for CAPABILITY_GAP. Everything else fell through to the resume and the waiter was dispatched as though its question had been answered. A resolver that asked for an observation and did not get one cannot continue, whatever the reason.

H and the nesting rule. Two resolvers are waiting at once; the one resumed is the exact capability that asked most recently, and only when its own prerequisite has spoken. Innermost first: the knowledge rule comes back before the procedure that was waiting on the rule.

E. The resumed resolver asks for the very thing that was just run for it. Re-reading it would be a fresh claim about the world made to satisfy a resolver that already had the answer, and repeating it is how a loop that cannot end begins. It ends closed instead.

goals.explicit_request: 주문했는데 받는 곳 주소를 바꿀 수 있나요?
goals.subject: CURRENT_ORDER
goals.evidence: 주문했는데 받는 곳 주소를 바꿀 수 있나요?

why: F. R1 waits on R2, R2 waits on R1. Detected on the second request by the same observation that catches a duplicate — this capability has already run — so there is one rule here, not two, and no cycle can complete a lap.

F, the whole reason CustomerGoalSet exists. One message, two ACTION goals, and the customer said which one is conditional. The nozzle request is resolved and ends at the registry's missing executor; the refund is NOT ATTEMPTED — no resolver is asked for it at all — because nothing in this runtime establishes that the first request cannot happen. The gap on the primary is the trap: it says what we cannot do and nothing about what the seller will do.
customer_message: 분무기 노즐이 파손돼서 왔어요. 노즐 부분만 따로 배송해 주세요. 노즐만 배송이 불가능하면 환불처리 해주세요.
customer_message_why: customer_message is WRITTEN, not assembled. The fallback clause 「노즐만 배송이 불가능하면」 appears in it VERBATIM and is the same string the relation carries as stated_condition — so the relationship is discoverable from the input rather than from the answer key. Joining the two explicit_requests would have produced an input with the condition missing, which is the one thing this row exists to test.
